title: Journalism minor
notes:
General Guidelines
- The minor is open to all degree-seeking Berkeley students.
- Students must declare the Journalism minor prior to the first day of classes in their Estimated Graduation Term (EGT).
- No more than one upper division course may be used to simultaneously fulfill requirements for a student's major and minor programs.
- All courses intended to fulfill minor requirements must be taken for letter-graded credit.
- Students are required to earn a C (2.00) average or higher in all courses that are used to complete requirements for the minor.
University Requirements are assigned as part of your major degree program. There are no additional requirements for completing a minor.
College Requirements are assigned as part of your major degree program. There are no additional requirements for completing a minor.

rule.text:
The Minor in Journalism requires completion of five courses.
Two of five courses are core courses and are required: JOURN 100: Introduction to News Reporting and JOURN 110: Introduction to Multimedia Storytelling.
Three of the five courses are electives. Students can choose three electives from many possible options. Currently offered electives include courses on Social Media Verification & Engagement, Audio Podcasting, Photojournalism, Digital Research & Investigative Journalism, Data Journalism, Media Ethics, and more.
